claim: Among the documents in the DOJ's Epstein Files Transparency Act release is an FBI FD-71A "Guardian" complaint-intake form (Data Set 9, Bates EFTA01249210 / EFTA00095297), dated April 23, 2021, recording a tip phoned in to the FBI's National Threat Operations Center on October 14, 2020. The caller — described as a former compliance employee of BGC Financial / Cantor Fitzgerald — alleged money laundering, Ponzi-scheme activity (a "global Ponzi share" scheme said to force 3,500+ employees to contribute 10% of earnings), and regulatory breaches by Howard Lutnick (now Commerce Secretary) through those firms, said Lutnick "used philanthropy as a smokescreen," and claimed to hold documents that "could link Lutnick to Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell" — including an assertion that Epstein "sold Lutnick a house for $10 ... through a trust fund." The form is logged "MONEY LAUNDERING – ZERO FILE," the FBI's intake notation for a complaint on which no case is opened, and is cross-referenced to the Epstein case file (50D-NY-3027571), which is how it surfaced in the production. The document records that the allegation was made; it is an uninvestigated tip, not a finding — no evidence has surfaced that the FBI pursued it.

notes: Sensitive but squarely on the public record (DS9; surfaced and reported via Public Citizen/Democracy Defenders' resignation demand and Daily Kos). Written to the 'attribute, don't adopt / separate primary fact from attributed conclusion' rule: the PRIMARY FACT is that this FD-71A intake form exists in the release with this title, date, and 'ZERO FILE' status; the ALLEGATIONS within are an uninvestigated complainant tip, asserted here as made, not as true. 'Zero file' = no FBI investigation opened. Complainant PII (name/phone/DOB) is redacted in the source scrub — not reproduced here. NB the caller's 'Epstein sold Lutnick a house for $10 through a trust fund' claim does NOT match the documented deed chain in 1998-lutnick-epstein-townhouse-001 (a $7.6M 1998 purchase from the Comet Trust); the two are cross-related but the '$10' figure is the tipster's unverified assertion, not the property record.
